bull_bear.body:
- Established "Ankur" brand in edible oils, with the Company in operation since its incorporation on 31 December 1992
- Location in Gujarat, described by the Company as one of the leading processors of cotton in the country, giving very good cottonseed raw-material availability
- Diversified product portfolio across cottonseed, soybean, sunflower, corn and mustard oils, which the Company states provides flexibility to respond to changes in consumer demand, raw material availability and market pricing
- In-house manufacturing know-how — the Company states its products are manufactured using in-house know how with no outside technology used
- Promoter-family management with long operating experience in the edible oil business (Whole-Time Director with 30 to 40 years in edible oil, including marketing and financing)
- All properties including buildings, plant and machinery and stocks are stated to be adequately insured
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material / commodity price risk — Raw material and commodity prices can be volatile due to crop conditions, weather, international commodity prices, supply-demand conditions and Government policies. The Company states that significant increases in raw material prices may adversely affect margins if corresponding increases in selling prices cannot be implemented — the structural core of a refining business whose principal raw material is edible and non-edible oil sourced from domestic markets at prices that generally track international levels.
- Margin / spread compression between procurement cost and realisation — The edible oil business is described as inherently sensitive to raw material and commodity-price movements, so maintaining the spread between procurement cost and selling price remains a key management focus. This risk was realised in FY 2025-26: the Company reports net profit margin declining from approximately 2.29% to 1.40% because material consumption rose faster than revenue.
- Competition risk — The edible oil market is competitive, with established national, regional and local brands present. The Company must continuously maintain product quality, competitive pricing and customer relationships, limiting its pricing power when input costs rise.
- Market price risk on inventory — Fluctuations in edible oil prices may affect inventory valuations, procurement costs and realisations. This is structurally significant given inventories rose from Rs 20.43 crore to Rs 38.67 crore during FY 2025-26, so a larger stock position is exposed to price movement.
- Working capital and liquidity risk — The business requires adequate working capital, particularly for inventory procurement and day-to-day operations, making efficient management of inventory, receivables and supplier credit important. Liquidity risk is separately defined in the notes as the risk that the company will not be able to settle or meet its obligations on time or at reasonable price, monitored by the treasury department through rolling cash-flow forecasts.
- Single-counterparty concentration — Ankur Oil Industries — A structural concentration disclosure rather than a labelled risk: Ankur Oil Industries, a related-party partnership firm in which several directors are common partners, is named as the single customer accounting for more than 10% of trade receivables at both 31 March 2026 and 31 March 2025, and is the Company's largest related-party sales counterparty. Concentration of both revenue and receivables in one related entity is a governance and credit risk. The auditors also flag existence and recoverability of trade receivables (Rs 1017.57 lakhs, 12.40% of total assets) as a Key Audit Matter.
- Regulatory risk — Changes in food safety regulations, taxation, import duties, Government policies and other applicable laws may affect the Company's operations and cost structure — import duty changes in particular move the landed cost of competing edible oils.
- Operational / single-site risk — Manufacturing operations are subject to risks relating to plant operations, utilities, equipment, maintenance, labour, logistics and availability of raw materials. The Company operates from a single refining facility at Changodar, Ahmedabad, so any disruption there is not geographically diversified away. The notes separately quantify sensitivity of borrowing cost to a 50-basis-point move on working capital facilities from banks and loans from directors, indicating floating-rate funding exposure alongside substantial promoter/director lending.

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no capex or capacity-expansion project. The Directors' Report states only that the Company's refining facility at Changodar, Ahmedabad has an installed refining capacity of approximately 110 tonnes of refined oil per day, with no addition, commissioning, debottlenecking or new-site plan named. Growth intent is framed entirely as better use of existing assets — the MD&A Outlook and Opportunities sections speak of improving capacity utilisation and operational efficiency rather than adding capacity, and the Directors' Report records that no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position occurred between the end of the financial year and the date of the report. The Company also states that no specific investment has been made in reduction of energy consumption, that its products are made using in-house know-how with no outside technology absorbed, and that it has no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company, so there is no inorganic capacity or geographic addition either. - Operational / single-site risk — Manufacturing operations are subject to risks relating to plant operations, utilities, equipment, maintenance, labour, logistics and availability of raw materials. The Company operates from a single refining facility at Changodar, Ahmedabad, so any disruption there is not geographically diversified away. The notes separately quantify sensitivity of borrowing cost to a 50-basis-point move on working capital facilities from banks and loans from directors, indicating floating-rate funding exposure alongside substantial promoter/director lending.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Focus on the core edible oil business — maintaining product quality, strengthening market presence and meeting evolving customer requirements
- Improve operating margins by optimising raw material procurement and maintaining spreads between procurement cost and selling prices
- Increase penetration of branded, packaged edible oil products and strengthen the Ankur brand
- Increase the contribution of diversified products — soybean, corn and mustard oils — alongside the dominant cottonseed oil
- Improve capacity utilisation and operational efficiency at the Changodar refining facility

hero.oneLiner: Ambar Protein Industries is an Ahmedabad-based edible-oil refiner selling refined cottonseed and other edible oils under its established "Ankur" brand from a Changodar refinery with a stated refining capacity of approximately 110 tonnes of refined oil per day.
